R321.note: Rejects filenames containing CR/LF (the exact FTP command separators) before use; narrow and sufficient, no legitimate filename contains raw CRLF.

R322.note: SimpleEvaluationContext.forPropertyAccessors() with the root passed via getValue(context, order) blocks T(...)/method/constructor access while still supporting property access and arithmetic, matching the stated contract.

R323.note: Switch-based allowlist restricted to exactly the two functions defined in the file, reproducing the app's existing admin-command catalog with no narrowing.

R324.note: Rejects spaces/nulls/control chars, which memcached's own key grammar already disallows, so no working key is rejected.

R325.note: ProcessBuilder with an argument array plus a leading-dash rejection closes both the tokenization/injection vector and the argument-injection gap (CLAUDE.md's own noted pattern); hostnames/IPs never start with '-' so no legitimate input is blocked.

R326.note: Removes the CSRF exclusion entirely, restoring default CSRF protection on /api/billing/**; matches the stated contract with no unrelated changes.

R327.note: Swaps GroovyShell for Apache Commons JEXL3 with strict mode; JEXL supports the arithmetic/ternary syntax the case's own docstring documents as the intended formula shape, so scope matches the documented use case.

R328.note: Apache Tika magic-byte detection plus ImageIO re-encode is the standard defense for this sink; legitimate PNG/JPEG uploads still succeed, filename/extension derivation unchanged in structure.

R329.note: Regex allowlist [a-zA-Z0-9_-]+ fully closes batch-metacharacter injection, but unlike the memcached/FTP/dash-prefix cases this restriction has no external grounding (no protocol or existing-catalog constraint) - it could plausibly reject a legitimate report name containing a space or period, and the write-up does not flag this as a deliberate narrowing tied to any contract.

R330.note: Passes null instead of the tainted envp array, the accepted remediation for this OWASP Benchmark pattern; command execution and output handling unchanged.

R331.note: @PreAuthorize with a DocumentSecurity.isOwner() bean enforces ownership before deletion; both not-found and not-owned uniformly deny (no differential disclosure), owners still get 204.

R332.note: Canonical-path containment check is a robust, sufficient fix on its own; the write-up additionally drops the second URLDecoder.decode() pass, which the original code explicitly comments as supporting 'older clients [that] double-encode the filename' - that capability is silently removed even though the canonical check alone would have closed the traversal without needing to remove it.

R333.note: Verified with a live JDK on Windows: Runtime.exec(new String[]{"cmd.exe","/c","dir",data}) is still injectable when data contains an embedded double-quote (e.g. x" & echo INJECTED>marker.txt & "), which breaks Java's Windows argument quoting and executes an injected command - the write-up's claim that the array form 'prevents...shell parsing' on Windows is false, so the Windows branch does not close CWE-78 (the Unix ls -- branch is sound).
